messages:
sylvia: Heads-up — customer asked for operator-level control over outbound routes for private deployments (per-tenant egress rules). They want to lock down which subnets and external destinations tenants can reach, and to do that without operator CLI hacks.
laura: Important for compliance. Do they mean agent-enforced policies or installer-provisioned network ACLs?
tim_r: leaning agent-enforced. Customers want policies shipped with the tenant config so upgrades preserve them.
derek: Agent-enforced is flexible but we need a clear permission model. Who can change the policy: tenant-admin or platform-admin?
sylvia: Quote from customer: "We need team A to only hit analytics.example.com and S3, but nothing else externally." So two scopes: per-tenant allowed destinations + operator-managed SNAT/IP pool.
jen: Operationally, this affects upgrade path: if we change how we implement egress (iptables vs eBPF vs cloud NAT), we must migrate existing policies without breaking traffic. Need migration plan.
laura: Agreed. Proposal: 1) declarative policy spec in operator CRD (yaml). 2) agent applies policy with a versioned schema. 3) migration shim for older installers.
tim_r: rough config example:```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: EgressPolicy
metadata:
  tenant: acme
spec:
  allowedDestinations:
    - dns: analytics.example.com
    - cidr: 10.0.0.0/24
  egressMode: SNAT
  snatPool: tenant-acme-pool
  enforcementVersion: v1
```
derek: enforcementVersion is critical. For v2 we might switch to L3 filters + eBPF. Keep enforcementVersion in CR so operator can rollout.
jen: How about UX? Console should show effective rules and a dry-run button. Also audit trail and who applied change (KMS-backed signing for operator overrides).
sylvia: On rollback: if enforcementVersion changes during an upgrade, default behavior should be "compat mode" where agent translates v1 rules to v2 until confirmed by operator. No sudden deny-by-default.
laura: Network owners also care about IP preservation. If SNAT pool changes we need a migration window and ephemeral mapping table so long-lived sessions don't drop.
tim_r: Performance note: eBPF path will be cheaper at scale but tighter kernel compatibility. For Private we must support config that falls back to iptables on older kernels.
derek: Define acceptance criteria for launch: 1) CRD v1 implemented + documented, 2) agent enforcer for iptables + optional eBPF, 3) migration shim tests, 4) console UI for viewing policies, 5) audit logs + RBAC hooks.
jen: Add a customer-driven acceptance: ability for tenant-admin to request a trimmed list of external FQDNs and get SLA on enforcement within X minutes.
sylvia: Action items: laura + tim to draft CRD and migration sketch by EOD Thu; derek + ops to prototype iptables shim; jen to scope console wireframe. I'll coordinate with acct team to capture exact customer SLAs.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist: create backlog ticket "egress-policy-crd" and link RFC doc.
laura: acked, starting draft. :+1:
jen: I'll mock a wireframe and share link tomorrow. :eyes:
tim_r: quick question — do we allow DNS-based rules (fqdn) long-term? It's messy with CDNs. Suggest supporting DNS on label + pinned IP ranges for critical services.
derek: DNS-fallback OK but note TTL churn. Add cache invalidation behavior to spec.
sylvia: Good point. Include "dnsResolutionPolicy" field in draft.
jen: Also flag: KMS integration for signing policy changes in Private deployments — compliance wants tamper evidence.
laura: Will include KMS notes.
ops-bot: ticket created: https://redwood.internal/board/INFR-5123
sylvia: Thanks — we'll sync again after drafts.
laura: ping me if you want a quick review before Thursday.
jen: Will post wireframe link when ready.
